==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per- (fare)}}
From {{inh|en|enm|reporten}}, from {{der|en|xno|reporter}}, from {{der|en|la|reporto|reportāre|to carry back, return, remit, refer}}, from {{af|la|re-|porto<alt:portāre>|nocat=1}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈpɔːt/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈpoɹt/|/ɹəˈpoɹt/|a=GenAm,CA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-report.ogg|a=California}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Wodencafe-report.wav|a=Texas}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Grendelkhan-report.wav|a=Connecticut}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈpoːt/|a=Australia}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɹəˈpoːt/|a=NZ}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈpo(ː)ɹt/|a=rhotic,non-horse-hoarse}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈpoət/|a=non-rhotic,non-horse-hoarse}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)t|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive}} To relate details of (an event or incident); to [[recount]], [[describe]] (something). {{defdate|from {{C.|15}}}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-01-01|author=Paul Bartel; Ashli Moore| volume=101| issue=1|page=47–48| magazine=w:American Scientist| title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/issues/feature/2013/1/avian-migration-the-ultimate-red-eye-flight Avian Migration: The Ultimate Red-Eye Flight]| passage=Many of these classic methods are still used, with some modern improvements. For example, with the aid of special microphones and automated sound detection software, ornithologists recently '''reported'''{{...}}that pine siskins (''Spinus pinus'') undergo an irregular, nomadic type of nocturnal migration.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[repeat]] (something one has heard), to [[retell]]; to [[pass on]], [[convey]] (a message, information etc.). {{defdate|from 15th c.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete|reflexive}} To take oneself ({{m|en|to}} someone or something) for guidance or support; to [[appeal]]. {{defdate|15th|18th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Mlry MrtDrthr|20.4|2|XVIII|ij|passage=thenne they ansuerd by and by that they coude not excuse the quene /{{...}}/ Allas sayd the quene I made this dyner for a good entente / and neuer for none euyl soo almyghty god me help in my ryght as I was neuer purposed to doo suche euylle dedes / and that I '''reporte''' me vnto god}}
# {{lb|en|formal|transitive}} To [[notify]] someone of (particular intelligence, suspicions, illegality, misconduct etc.); to make notification to relevant authorities; to submit a formal report of. {{defdate|from 15th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|For insurance reasons, I had to '''report''' the theft to the local police station.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To make a formal [[statement]], especially of complaint, about (someone). {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|If you do that again I'll '''report''' you to the boss.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To show up or appear at an appointed time; to present oneself. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To write [[news]] [[report]]s (for); to [[cover]] as a [[journalist]] or [[reporter]]. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|Andrew Marr '''reports''' now on more in-fighting at Westminster.}}
#: {{ux|en|Every newspaper '''reported''' the war.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be accountable to or [[subordinate]] to (someone) in a [[hierarchy]]; to [[receive]] [[order]]s from (someone); to give [[official]] [[update]]s to (someone who is above oneself in a hierarchy).
#: {{ux|en|The financial director '''reports''' to the CEO.}}
#: {{ux|en|Now that I've been promoted, I '''report to''' Benjamin, whom I loathe.}}
#* {{quote-web|en|title=Who Is Barret Zoph? Co-Founder of $12B AI Startup Fired after CEO Mira Murati Learns of Office Affair as Both Lovebirds Go Back to OpenAI|author=R. Ghosh|date=January 22, 2026|url=https://www.ibtimes.sg/who-barret-zoph-co-founder-12b-ai-startup-fired-after-ceo-mira-murati-learns-office-affair-83390|work=w:International Business Times|passage=Although she was junior to {{quote-gloss|Barret}} Zoph, the report said that she did not '''report''' directly to him.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260215111949/https://www.ibtimes.sg/who-barret-zoph-co-founder-12b-ai-startup-fired-after-ceo-mira-murati-learns-office-affair-83390|archivedate=15 February 2026}}
# {{lb|en|politics|dated}} To return or present as the result of an examination or consideration of any matter officially referred.
#: {{ux|en|The committee '''reported''' the bill with amendments, or '''reported''' a new bill, or '''reported''' the results of an inquiry.}}
# To take [[minutes]] of (a speech, the doings of a public body, etc.); to write down from the lips of a speaker.
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[refer]].
#* {{RQ:Fuller Holy Warre|chapter=Baldwine the Fourth Succeedeth; His Education under William the Reverend Archbishop of Tyre|page=94|passage=Baldwine his ſonne, the fourth of that name [{{w|Baldwin IV of Jerusalem}}], ſucceeded his father [{{w|Amalric of Jerusalem}}]: ſo like unto him, that we '''report''' the reader to the character of King Almerick, and will ſpare the repeating his description.}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive|obsolete|rare}} To return or repeat, as sound; to echo.
#* {{RQ:Bacon Sylva Sylvarum|passage=a church with windows only from above{{...}} that '''reporteth''' the voice twelve or thirteen times}}
# {{lb|en|nautical}} Of a ship, to return to a [[port]].
#: {{ux|en|Our ship leaves port on Monday and will '''re-port''' on Friday.}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A piece of information describing, or an [[account]] of certain [[event]]s given or presented to someone, with the most common [[adposition]]s being [[by]] (referring to creator of the report) and [[on]] (referring to the subject).
#: {{ux|en|A '''report''' by the telecommunications ministry on the phone network revealed a severe capacity problem.}}
# [[reputation|Reputation]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Sonnets|36||I love thee in such sort / As, thou being mine, mine is thy good '''report'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1902|author=John Buchan|title=The Outgoing of the Tide
|passage=Certain it is that if he had been daft before, he now ran wild in his pranks, and an evil '''report''' of him was in every mouth.}}
# {{lb|en|firearms}} The [[sharp]], loud sound of a [[gunshot]] or explosion.
#* {{RQ:Melville Moby-Dick|The Cabin Table|166|While their masters, the mates, seemed afraid of the sound of the hinges of their own jaws, the harpooneers chewed their food with such a relish that there was a '''report''' to it.}}
#* {{RQ:Stevenson Treasure Island|text={{...}} a pistol-shot, flash and '''report''', came from the hedge-side.}}
#* {{RQ:Burroughs Return of Tarzan|passage=Waziri’s warriors marched at a rapid trot through the jungle in the direction of the village. For a few minutes, the sharp cracking of guns ahead warned them to haste, but finally the '''reports''' dwindled to an occasional shot, presently ceasing altogether.}}
# {{lb|en|business}} An [[employee]] whose position in a [[corporate]] hierarchy is below that of a particular manager.
#: {{synonyms|en|subordinate}}
#* {{RQ:FT|edition=weekend|author=Madeleine Speed; Mercedes Ruehl|date=2025-09-20|title=The meltdown at Nestlé|page=6|passage=The revelation that boss of one year Laurent Freixe was conducting an undisclosed affair with a direct '''report''' has rocked a 159-year-old conglomerate that pioneered infant formula and milk chocolate before growing to become the world's largest food and beverage company.}}
